name: Postiz
tagline: Social media scheduler for 28+ channels with AI assistance and team features

pricing.notes: Official pricing checked 2026-07-30; Standard at $29/month with 5 channels, Team $39, Pro $49, Ultimate $99.

tiers.name: Standard
tiers.limits: 5 connected channels, solo use, 20 AI images/month, 3 AI videos/month, 2 webhooks
tiers.notes: The pricing card says unlimited posts, while the official homepage FAQ says Standard includes 400 posts/month; this unresolved first-party contradiction is preserved.

tiers.name: Team
tiers.limits: 10 connected channels, unlimited posts and team members, 100 AI images/month, 10 AI videos/month, 10 webhooks

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: 30 connected channels, unlimited posts/team members, 300 AI images/month, 30 AI videos/month, 30 webhooks

tiers.name: Ultimate
tiers.limits: 100 connected channels, unlimited posts/team members/webhooks, 500 AI images/month, 60 AI videos/month

pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual (vendor says about 20% off, but exact annual USD amounts were not exposed); 7-day hosted trial
pricing.hiddenCosts: Self-hosting avoids the Postiz subscription but still requires infrastructure and, for some networks, developer-app approval/API costs. Hosted AI image/video allowances are capped; unused allowance treatment and overage prices are not public.

verdictSummary: The core loop (compose, queue, cron tick, publish) is one-shottable for networks with open APIs like Mastodon, Bluesky, and Telegram. What you cannot one-shot is the reason schedulers exist as products: OAuth apps for Instagram, LinkedIn, TikTok, and X are approval-gated or paid, and keeping 28+ integrations alive as platforms change policies is permanent maintenance. Postiz is also fully open source, so the honest DIY move for the full feature set is self-hosting it rather than rebuilding it.
coreLoopDIY: Compose posts into a slot-based queue, publish them on schedule to open-API networks via per-network adapters, and log outcomes.
whatYouLose: pre-approved platform OAuth apps (Instagram, LinkedIn, TikTok)
whyPeopleStillPay: The hosted version ships with platform-approved OAuth apps, so connecting Instagram, LinkedIn, or TikTok is a click instead of a developer-app review process. Social APIs break and change terms constantly; paying outsources that upkeep plus analytics, teams, and AI features.

priorArt.name: Postiz (open source)
priorArt.desc: The app itself is AGPL open source and self-hostable, which is the shortest path to the full feature set.

alternatives.name: Postiz
alternatives.desc: The paid service is the hosted edition of this exact open-source product; keep the features and inherit the stack.

notes: Rare case where the SaaS is its own prior art · self-host it instead of rebuilding it.
prompt:
Build me a personal social post scheduler to replace Postiz. Requirements:

- Node + Express + better-sqlite3; a localhost page with a compose box,
  image attach, and the queue ordered by send time.
- Three targets: Mastodon (access token), Bluesky (app password via
  @atproto/api), and a Telegram channel (bot token). Creds in .env, one
  small adapter file per network so a fourth is addable later.
- Slot-based queueing: I define posting times per weekday in my timezone
  and new posts fill the next free slot; a post can also be pinned to an
  exact datetime or duplicated across networks with per-network text.
- A node-cron tick every minute publishes due posts, marks each row sent
  or failed, retries failures 3 times with backoff, and marks before
  sending so nothing ever double-posts.
- Per-network character counter in the composer; attached images stored
  in media/ next to the database, resized to each network's limits with
  sharp.
- A history page of the last 100 sent posts linking to the live posts.
- Runs on my always-on box; localhost only, no accounts, no telemetry.
- Out of scope: Instagram, LinkedIn, TikTok, and X (approval-gated or
  paid APIs, say so in the README), analytics, teams, and AI features.
- README: getting a Mastodon token, a Bluesky app password, and a
  Telegram bot token.
